_comment: The closed vocabulary the corrections log is checked against.
SHIPPED EMPTY, ON PURPOSE. The origin project's twelve classes are its own
earned evidence, and `corrections_log` requires every declared value to be
USED by some entry -- copying that file into a fresh repo produces one
violation per unused class (18 of them, measured 2026-08-02). That is not the
gate being awkward; it is the gate enforcing the rule that a value list nobody
uses is how a closed list quietly becomes an open one.
So a class arrives with the first entry that needs it. Adding one is a
deliberate edit to this file, which is exactly the visibility that keeps the
list closed -- and it means your vocabulary describes YOUR failures rather
`gate` and `disposition` are the framework's own axes and are not usage-
checked, so they ship filled in. Do not edit them to make a run pass; that is

class.derived-what-only-the-act-knew: a fact recomputed from the current state that only the original action could know -- the recomputation is indistinguishable from the truth until the two diverge
class.origin-repo-had-it-by-hand: the framework's own checkout satisfied a requirement by hand, so the install step that was supposed to produce it in a consuming project was never noticed missing
class.work-printed-instead-of-done: a tool that ends by printing the work it should have performed -- correct as a list of next actions, wrong about who acts
class.schema-field-nothing-read: a config field written, validated and documented while no code path consumes it -- acceptance by the schema is the evidence a maintainer uses to conclude it is wired up
class.derived-not-verified: a rule reasoned out carefully, written down confidently, and wrong the first time reality touched it -- the code implementing it correct in every case
class.origin-identity-baked-in: the framework hardcodes something that is TRUE OF THE REPO IT WAS EXTRACTED FROM and false everywhere else -- a name, a handle, a path, a citation. The inverse of origin-repo-had-it-by-hand: not a property the origin repo satisfies so the tool was never asked to produce it, but the origin repo's identity carried inside the tool. Structurally invisible from the origin checkout, where every such string reads as correct, so no gate, test or reviewer that runs there can see it
class.guards-composed-into-a-prohibition: two guards on the same tool, each individually correct and each fully covered by its own tests, whose denial sets intersect to forbid an operation neither one was written to forbid. Visible from no single site: a guard cannot see the others, so each test suite can ask 'does this deny what it should' and none can ask 'what is left possible once every guard has run'. The symptom is a MISSING action rather than a wrong one, and nothing observes an action nobody attempts -- so it surfaces when a human asks for the capability, not when a gate fires
class.new-member-met-old-membership-tests: a new member of an existing set -- a ref namespace, an outcome enum, a lane list -- is picked up automatically by every site that matches the set BY PATTERN and silently skipped by every site that ENUMERATES its members, so adding one both extends behaviour nobody chose and removes behaviour nobody noticed going. Invisible in the diff, because the sites that decide are all code the change never touched
class.category-of-one-read-as-a-literal: a category with exactly one member is indistinguishable from a hardcoded string, so its consumers each spell that member out instead of asking the category -- and when a second member arrives every consumer has to be recalled from memory rather than found by following a reference. The near-inverse of new-member-met-old-membership-tests: there the set exists and enumerating sites skip the newcomer, here THE SET WAS NEVER NAMED, so there is nothing for a new member to be added to and no site a search can lead you to. Undetectable while the count is one, because every literal is correct and the duplication looks like coincidence
class.reported-into-a-channel-nobody-read: a mechanism reported on itself correctly, into a destination with no reader -- a stream sent to DEVNULL, a message shown by code that then reloads the page. The report exists, is accurate and is complete, so every test of the reporting passes; what fails is the last hop, which no test observes because it is a human eye. Distinct from silent-noop (the work does happen) and from unbounded-wait-read-as-progress (there is output, it just lands nowhere). Discarding a channel is always an implicit claim that SOMETHING ELSE reports, and the tell is that the claim names a mechanism rather than a file and a writer: 'progress is read from the files the command already writes' is true of whichever command it was written for and unexamined for the five that inherited the code
class.unbounded-wait-read-as-progress: a step that can block forever was given no ceiling, so its failure emits no output and no exit code -- and since that is precisely what a long-running SUCCESS looks like from outside, the reasonable response (wait a bit more) is the wrong one, and stays wrong indefinitely. Distinct from silent-noop and from check-stopped-checking: nothing is reported as success, nothing is reported at all, and the check would have been perfectly correct had it ever returned. The tell is a human asking 'is it stuck or just slow?' -- a question the tool should have answered and cannot, because answering it requires a bound nobody set
class.delegated-the-write-kept-none-of-its-boo: a caller that used to perform a file write itself hands the write to an agent, and the bookkeeping that surrounded the write in every non-delegated sibling -- the commit, the stamp, the receipt -- ends up owned by nobody: the agent was never told about it, and the caller no longer touches the files it would have hung the bookkeeping off. Invisible from both sides, because each is complete in its own terms. The tell is a sibling comparison that comes out even on the WORK and uneven on the RECORD of it
class.ambient-environment-assumed-not-resolved: a repo that owns a resolver for some ambient fact -- where an executable lives, which config directory is in force -- has one call site that hands the question to the environment instead: a bare command name given to a shell, a relative path given to a subprocess. Invisible because every caller that asks the resolver asks for a REASON -- it needs the value to build an argv it assembles itself -- while the delegating one has no such moment, so the resolution never presents itself as a step being skipped. Compounded when the spawn's exit code is deliberately unread, which is usual for the detached windows and background jobs where this shape lives: the failure then surfaces only to whoever happens to be looking at the window

channel.maintainer: the framework's maintainer, reading or running it
channel.gate: a gate in this repo caught it, on a real tree rather than a fixture
channel.claude: an agent found it while doing something else, usually by running it
channel.test: a test caught it -- and the entries that use this are worth reading together, because a test finding a defect it was not written for is the strongest evidence the test earned its place

gate.yes: an existing gate would have failed on this
gate.yes-now: a gate built or fixed as a result of this correction now catches it
gate.no-judgment: genuinely needs human or LLM judgment, not pattern-matching
gate.no-gap: mechanically catchable in principle, but no gate exists yet
gate.n/a: not a defect, so the question does not apply -- a baseline, a measurement or a recorded decision

disposition.gate: closed by a gate now enforcing it -- pointer names the gate module
disposition.recipe: closed by a recipe or skill change -- pointer names the recipe/skill file
disposition.commit: closed by a specific code or doc change with no gate/recipe of its own -- pointer is a commit sha or short description of the change
disposition.doc: closed by a memory or plan-doc correction -- pointer names the doc
disposition.no-action: deliberately left open by judgment rather than by an oversight -- pointer states the reason acting further is not warranted
